metaDescription: Compare six 20V cordless hedge trimmers by blade length, cut capacity, weight and battery platform, with picks for small yards and big hedge rows.
expertTake: The BLACK+DECKER LHT2220 is the pick for most homeowners because it pairs a 22 inch dual-action blade with a full kit and a platform you can service anywhere. The WORX WG261 is the value-minded alternative if you already own other PowerShare tools. If your hedges are thick, woody privet or overgrown laurel with stems past three quarters of an inch, skip the 20V class and buy a 40V or 56V trimmer or a gas unit instead.
introParagraphs: A cordless hedge trimmer is a pair of reciprocating blades driven by a small motor and gearbox, and the box numbers rarely tell you how it will behave in a real hedge. Blade length, strokes per minute and battery size all get printed in bold, but the stems you are cutting care about blade gap, motor torque and how long the battery holds voltage under load.

This guide explains how to read those numbers, what separates a trimmer that finishes a boxwood row from one that stalls on a single privet branch, and how battery platform choice affects the next ten years of ownership. Start with the picks above for a quick shortlist, then read the individual reviews below for the tradeoffs.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER LHT2220 20V MAX 22 Inch Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
The LHT2220 is the least surprising trimmer in this group, and that is a compliment. A 22 inch dual-action blade means both cutting edges move, so the blade pair shears from two directions and the trimmer vibrates less than a single-action design running the same stroke. That cuts fatigue noticeably on a long hedge row, because vibration, not weight, is what wears out your forearms first.

The 3/4 inch cutting capacity is the useful figure here. It lets the blade gap swallow typical new growth on privet, boxwood, yew and forsythia without stalling, and it matches the Craftsman 20 inch pick on capacity while giving you two more inches of reach per pass. Next to the 18 inch BLACK+DECKER LHT218C1 in this roundup, it covers roughly one fifth more hedge per sweep, which adds up on a fifty foot run.

Ownership is simple. The 20V MAX platform is one of the most widely stocked in the country, so replacement batteries and chargers are easy to find years from now. Keep the blades clean, wipe them with a light oil after each session and store the trimmer with the blade cover on. The included battery is modest, so a large property wants a second pack.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with a mixed set of hedges who want a dependable, full-kit trimmer without platform risk.
pros: Dual-action blade keeps vibration down over long hedge runs
22 in blade covers more hedge per pass than 18 and 20 in rivals
3/4 in capacity handles ordinary new growth without stalling
Battery and charger are included, so it works out of the box
cons: Single included battery limits runtime on large properties
Not built for woody stems past its rated capacity
Brushed motor draws more battery than brushless designs

products.name: WORX WG261 20V 22 Inch Cordless Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
WORX built this trimmer around a D-grip handle, which changes how you hold the tool. Instead of a fixed pistol grip behind a wrap-around handle, the D-grip lets you rotate your wrist to cut flat tops, vertical faces and low ground-level growth without shifting your stance. For people who trim at awkward angles, that flexibility matters more than another half pound of weight.

At about 5.5 pounds with the battery, it is heavier than the 4 pound Banmiip, and the 2.0Ah pack is a small tank for a 22 inch blade. Expect to finish a modest hedge on one charge and need a swap for anything longer. The 3/4 inch blade gap matches the BLACK+DECKER LHT2220, so cutting capacity is a wash, and the real differentiator is the battery ecosystem.

PowerShare is the reason to pick this one. The same 20V pack runs a large family of WORX garden and power tools, and some 40V tools accept adapters, so one set of batteries covers the trimmer, a blower and a string trimmer. If you have no WORX tools, the ecosystem value disappears and the BLACK+DECKER is the easier buy. Oil the blades after use and keep the vents clear of clippings.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who already own or plan to buy several PowerShare tools and want one battery for all of them.
pros: D-grip handle lets you cut in any orientation without repositioning
One 20V battery fits a large family of garden tools
3/4 in blade gap matches the best capacity in this group
Overmolded grips damp vibration well on long sessions
cons: The 2.0Ah battery is small for a 22 in blade
Heavier than the compact tool-only options here
Value shrinks if you own no other PowerShare tools

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 CMCHT810C1 20 Inch Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
Craftsman's V20 trimmer is the compact middle option: a 20 inch dual-action steel blade that still carries the 3/4 inch capacity of the 22 inch models. The shorter blade gives up two inches per pass against the BLACK+DECKER LHT2220, but it is easier to control around corners and tight topiary, where a long blade overshoots.

The included 1.5Ah battery is the smallest in this roundup, and runtime reflects that. It suits a quick weekend tidy of foundation shrubs or a short privacy hedge. If you have more than a couple of dozen feet of hedge, plan to buy a bigger V20 pack, which also works across the Craftsman 20V line.

The integrated hook is a small but real convenience. It lets you hang the trimmer on a wall track or a garage nail, which keeps the blade off the floor and the cover on. Ownership is easy: clean and oil the blade, charge the battery before storing it for winter, and avoid leaving it in a hot shed, because heat is what ages lithium packs fastest.
products.bestFor: Owners of small to medium hedges who value a shorter, more controllable blade and compact wall storage.
pros: 20 in blade is more manageable on corners and shaped shrubs
3/4 in capacity matches the 22 in models
Built-in hook makes wall hanging easy
Works with other V20 batteries and tools
cons: The 1.5Ah battery gives the shortest runtime here
Fewer inches per pass than the 22 in trimmers

products.name: BLACK+DECKER LHT218C1 20V MAX 18 Inch Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
This is the small-yard answer in the lineup. An 18 inch blade with a 5/8 inch capacity is sized for boxwood balls, foundation shrubs and a short privacy screen, not a long property line. Its 2,400 cuts per minute is a respectable stroke rate that keeps the blades moving quickly through light growth, which gives a clean finish on soft stems.

The tradeoff is capacity. At 5/8 inch it gives up an eighth of an inch to the LHT2220 and the Craftsman, which is the difference between slicing through a thumb-thick stem and bogging down on it. Keep it for annual shaping, not catch-up work on overgrown hedges.

Handling is where it shines for new users. The T-handle and full-length trigger let you hold it in several positions, and the electric start means no pull cords or priming. Because it shares the 20V MAX platform with the LHT2220, a spare battery moves between the two. Clean it after every use and check the blade bolts for looseness once a season.
products.bestFor: Small yards and light shaping jobs where a shorter blade and easy handling matter more than reach.
pros: Shorter blade is easy to control around shaped shrubs
2,400 cuts per minute gives a clean finish on soft growth
T-handle and full-length trigger suit several grip positions
Shares batteries with the larger 20V MAX trimmer
cons: 5/8 in capacity limits it on woody stems
Covers less hedge per pass than the 22 in models

products.name: YDlawn 20V 22 Inch Hedge Trimmer with Two 4.0Ah Batteries
products.description:
YDlawn answers the runtime complaint by shipping two 4.0Ah packs and a fast charger with a 22 inch dual-action trimmer. Total stored energy is well over double the small packs bundled with the Craftsman and WORX kits, and swapping a fresh pack in mid-job means you can finish a long hedge without waiting on the charger.

Laser-cut blades are machined to a consistent edge and tend to cut cleaner than stamped blades out of the box. That helps right away, though how the edge holds up over seasons depends on the steel and heat treatment, which the listing does not detail. Treat this as a good-value kit and keep the blades clean and oiled.

The risk with a lesser-known brand is long-term parts support. Batteries are proprietary to the platform, so confirm you can buy a replacement pack before committing. It is the pick for someone with a big hedge who wants the most runtime in one box, but it is a less certain bet than BLACK+DECKER if you plan to keep it a decade.
products.bestFor: Larger hedges where long runtime in the box matters more than brand ecosystem.
pros: Two 4.0Ah batteries give the most runtime in this roundup
Fast charger shortens waiting between packs
Laser-cut 22 in blade cuts cleanly out of the box
Dual-button start and hand guard add safety
cons: Proprietary packs make long-term battery supply less certain
Less established parts and support than larger brands

products.name: Banmiip 22 Inch Hedge Trimmer for DeWalt 20V Batteries (Tool Only)
products.description:
This is a bare tool built to ride on DeWalt 20V MAX batteries, so it is only a sensible buy if you already own those packs. At about 4 pounds without a battery it is the lightest 22 inch trimmer in the group, and adding a typical pack brings it near the weight of the others. The 180 degree rotating rear handle makes vertical and horizontal cuts more comfortable.

Stroke rate is 2,000 per minute, lower than the 2,400 on the BLACK+DECKER 18 inch, and capacity is 2/3 inch, a notch under the 3/4 inch leaders. That means it is built for the same soft growth as the others and not for woody stems. Do not expect brushless-level torque from a trimmer that leans on a third-party design.

The real appeal is cost and convenience for DeWalt owners, who reuse existing batteries and skip a second charger. The caveat is that third-party tools on a brand's battery platform can have looser fit and no manufacturer support if the battery interface wears. Check the pack seats firmly, and avoid it if you want a single warranty covering tool and battery.
products.bestFor: Owners of DeWalt 20V MAX batteries who want a light bare-tool hedge trimmer and no extra charger.

180 degree rear handle eases vertical and horizontal cuts

cons: No battery or charger included, so the total outlay rises if you need them

buyingCriteria.explanation: A longer blade covers more hedge per pass but is harder to hold level and steer around curves, because the leverage at the tip grows with length. For flat-faced hedges and long straight runs, 22 inches is efficient, while shaped shrubs and tight corners reward 18 to 20 inches. A common mistake is buying the longest blade assuming it is always faster, then fighting wobble on topiary. In this lineup the BLACK+DECKER LHT2220 at 22 inches covers the most ground, while the LHT218C1 at 18 inches is the most precise.

Cut capacity is the maximum stem thickness the blade gap can accept before the stem pushes the blades apart instead of shearing. Most 20V trimmers top out at 5/8 to 3/4 inch, and cutting beyond that stalls the motor and wears the gearbox. Buyers often assume a trimmer cuts any branch it can fit between the teeth, but it does not. The LHT2220, WORX WG261 and Craftsman V20 all list 3/4 inch, while the LHT218C1 lists 5/8 inch and the Banmiip lists 2/3 inch.

Runtime depends on amp-hours, and a 20V trimmer draws steadily under load, so a 1.5Ah pack lasts about a third as long as a 4.0Ah pack. A short blade on a small hedge may finish on one charge, while 50 feet of dense privet will not. Buyers frequently overlook the bundled battery size and then find a trimmer that dies halfway through. The YDlawn ships with two 4.0Ah packs, the Craftsman only a 1.5Ah pack, so total energy differs by more than double.

A 20V pack is an investment because it fits an entire tool family, and the right choice is the platform that already covers your tools. BLACK+DECKER, WORX PowerShare and Craftsman V20 each have broad ranges, and the DeWalt-compatible Banmiip lets DeWalt owners reuse packs. Buying a trimmer on a new platform for a small saving ends up costing more in batteries and chargers. Consider what you will be mowing, blowing and trimming with in five years, not just this season.

Trimming happens at arm's length, often overhead, so the weight and vibration you feel in minute twenty matter more than the spec on paper. Dual-action blades cut vibration by moving both edges in opposite directions, and overmolded grips absorb what remains. Under five pounds is comfortable for most people, and the Banmiip at about 4 pounds bare is the lightest, while the WORX WG261 at 5.5 pounds is the heaviest. Always add the battery's weight to the stated tool weight.

Hedge trimmer blades can cause serious cuts, so a two-handed start, a hand guard and a blade cover are worth more than a few extra strokes per minute. The wrap-around handle design lets you hold the trimmer with both hands without reaching near the blades, and the cover protects both you and the edge in storage. The Banmiip and YDlawn both use dual-switch or dual-button starts, and the LHT2220's wrap-around handle gives secure two-hand control. Never trim overhead with a ladder unless you have secure footing.

specDecoder.meaning: This is how many times the blade pair completes a full back-and-forth cycle each minute. A higher rate gives a cleaner cut on soft stems because the blades pass a stem more frequently as you advance. It does not equal torque, so a fast trimmer can still stall on thick wood.
specDecoder.watchFor: Some brands quote no-load rates, which fall under cutting load. The LHT218C1's 2,400 and the Banmiip's 2,000 are free-running figures, not working speeds.

specDecoder.meaning: The widest stem the blade gap can accept and still shear cleanly. It is set by the spacing of the teeth, and cutting beyond it forces the stem between the teeth. Most 20V trimmers list 5/8 to 3/4 inch.
specDecoder.watchFor: Some listings round up or quote the gap without noting woody stems cut slower. Treat 3/4 inch as a limit for green growth, not for seasoned wood.

specDecoder.meaning: Amp-hours measure how much charge a battery stores. At 20V, a 4.0Ah pack holds twice the energy of a 2.0Ah pack, and the trimmer will run roughly twice as long under similar load.
specDecoder.watchFor: Runtime claims depend on conditions. The 1.5Ah Craftsman and 4.0Ah YDlawn kits differ by far more than their listings suggest in actual yard time.

specDecoder.meaning: The 20V MAX label refers to the peak voltage of a freshly charged pack with five cells in series, about 20 volts at full charge, with a nominal voltage closer to 18 volts under load. It is a marketing convention, and 18V and 20V MAX packs are the same cell count.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not assume 20V means more power than an 18V tool. It does not. Check the motor and amp-hours instead.

specDecoder.meaning: A bare tool ships without battery or charger, relying on your existing packs. It cuts cost for people already on a platform and saves weight at purchase.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Banmiip is bare and the others are kits. Compare total cost including packs before calling it the cheaper option.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capacity and blade geometry
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated cut capacity, blade length and whether the blades are dual-action. Capacity was weighted heavily because it limits which hedges a trimmer can actually handle. The LHT2220, WORX and Craftsman all lead at 3/4 inch, while the LHT218C1 sits at 5/8 inch.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at amp-hours, number of packs and charger speed for each kit. We then scored how much hedge a buyer could plausibly finish before waiting for a charge. The YDlawn's two 4.0Ah packs lead, and the Craftsman's single 1.5Ah pack trails.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and ergonomics
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated weights, handle layout and vibration control, adding a typical battery to bare-tool weights. Handle geometry that lets you hold the trimmer at several angles scored higher. The WORX D-grip and the Banmiip's rotating rear handle stood out.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how widely stocked each battery system is, how easy replacement packs are to find and whether a warranty covers tool and battery. Established platforms like BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX and WORX PowerShare scored higher than lesser-known systems.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read patterns in owner feedback rather than individual scores, looking for repeated mentions of blade dulling, battery failure or stalling on thick stems. Where a model's spec sheet and owner feedback disagreed, we favored the pattern in owner feedback and flagged the gap.

cards.label: Dual-action
cards.text: Both blades move in opposite directions, so the shearing force cancels and the trimmer vibrates less. It also cuts on both strokes, which gives a cleaner finish. Every trimmer in this roundup uses dual-action blades, including the BLACK+DECKER LHT2220, WORX WG261, Craftsman V20 and YDlawn.

cards.label: Single-action
cards.text: One blade moves while the other stays fixed. It is cheaper to build and heavier on vibration, because the moving blade creates all the reaction force. It is rarely found on 20V models today, and none of the picks here use it.

howToChoose.note: For almost every homeowner, dual-action is the right choice, and the only reason to consider single-action is a very low cost.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 22 in blade, 3/4 in capacity and at least 4.0Ah of battery. Long rows run through a small battery fast, and a blade under 20 inches means more passes. Dual-action blades and a wrap-around handle matter for control.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The BLACK+DECKER LHT2220 has the right blade and capacity but a modest battery, so pair it with a second pack. The YDlawn 22 in kit ships with two 4.0Ah packs, which makes it the stronger runtime choice. The Craftsman gives up reach for storage convenience.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your hedges include stems past 3/4 inch, you trim often or you want a longer warranty. The BLACK+DECKER LHT2220 on a bigger battery or a step up to a 40V trimmer will cut thicker growth with less stalling, and an established platform keeps batteries available for years.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim a few shrubs once or twice a year. The Craftsman CMCHT810C1 or the BLACK+DECKER LHT218C1 do that job, and the Banmiip is the cheap path if you already own DeWalt packs.

maintenance.why: Sap and clippings gum up the blade edges and increase friction. A light machine oil keeps the blades sliding and prevents rust.
Vibration slowly loosens the blade assembly screws. Loose blades cut poorly and can damage the gearbox.
Lithium packs age fastest when stored empty or hot. Keep them partly charged and indoors.
Clippings block the vents and cause overheating. A quick brush or blast of air solves it.
Dull blades tear stems and bog the motor. A fine file touches up minor nicks, and worn blades need replacement.

faq.q: Is a 22 inch or 18 inch blade better?
faq.a: It depends on the hedge. A 22 inch blade covers more per pass and suits long, flat runs, while an 18 inch blade is easier to steer around shaped shrubs and tight corners. Most homeowners with a mixed yard prefer 20 to 22 inches.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a 20V hedge trimmer?
faq.a: Expect to pay little for a basic kit and more for brushless motors or bigger batteries. For most yards, a mid-range kit with a 22 inch blade and a spare battery gives the best value. Count batteries in the total cost.

faq.q: How long do 20V hedge trimmer batteries last?
faq.a: Runtime depends on amp-hours and load, and a 1.5Ah pack may finish only a small hedge while a 4.0Ah pack runs several times longer. Lithium packs typically give several hundred charge cycles when stored cool and partly charged.

faq.q: Does 20V MAX mean more power than 18V?
faq.a: No. 20V MAX is a marketing label for the peak voltage of a fresh pack, and 18V and 20V MAX packs use the same number of cells. Compare motor type, amp-hours and cut capacity instead.

faq.q: Can a 20V trimmer cut thick branches?
faq.a: Only up to its rated capacity, usually 5/8 to 3/4 inch. Thicker branches should be cut with loppers or a pruning saw. Forcing a trimmer through wood can strip the gearbox.

faq.q: Is it safe to trim in wet conditions?
faq.a: Avoid trimming wet hedges and never use a battery trimmer in rain. Wet clippings clog blades and wet hands increase the risk of slipping. Always wear eye protection and gloves, and keep both hands on the handles.
